module.title: Bacterial lipopolysaccharide transport
module.description: Reusable module for ATP-driven extraction of lipopolysaccharide (LPS) from the outer leaflet of the inner membrane of diderm bacteria, its transfer across the periplasm along the trans-envelope Lpt protein bridge, and its insertion into the outer leaflet of the outer membrane. The module separates the LptB2FGC inner-membrane extraction machine, the soluble LptA bridge, and the LptD/LptE outer-membrane translocon, which together form the seven-protein lipopolysaccharide transport system.

module.notes: Scope and taxonomy. The Lpt system is present in diderm bacteria that build an LPS outer leaflet: all seven components were defined and characterized in Escherichia coli K-12, and orthologues are found across Proteobacteria and other LPS-bearing phyla (PANTHER reference trees include Chlamydia, Bacteroides, Leptospira, Aquifex and cyanobacteria). The module therefore uses E. coli K-12 as the primary experimental exemplar and Pseudomonas putida KT2440 as a second, independently curated exemplar. It is lineage-specific: monoderm bacteria (Bacillus subtilis), mycobacteria and Rhodococcus, which build mycolate rather than LPS outer layers, and eukaryotes lack the Lpt system, so no members are listed for them. Homologues in diderms without canonical LPS (Deinococcus, Thermotoga) are untested and are discussed in the family reviews. P. putida PP_0982 and PP_0983 encode LptF and LptG but lack lpt gene symbols in UniProt. MsbA flipping of LPS across the inner membrane, LPS biosynthesis, and core/O-antigen assembly are upstream and outside this transport module.

document.description: LptA is an essential, signal-peptide-bearing periplasmic protein of the seven-component lipopolysaccharide transport (Lpt) machinery of Escherichia coli. Its mature chain folds into a twisted beta-jellyroll with a hydrophobic groove, and it binds LPS through the lipid A moiety. LptA docks by its N-terminal edge onto the C-terminal edge of the beta-jellyroll of the inner-membrane protein LptC, and by its C-terminal edge onto the N-terminal periplasmic domain of the outer-membrane translocon LptD. One or a few head-to-tail LptA molecules thereby complete a continuous trans-envelope protein bridge. LPS extracted from the inner membrane by the ATP-driven LptB2FG transporter is passed from LptC to LptA and along the bridge to LptDE, which inserts it into the outer leaflet of the outer membrane. Bridge assembly is gated by correct LptDE assembly, and LptA is unstable when the bridge cannot form. Depletion of LptA blocks LPS delivery to the outer membrane, causes LPS to accumulate in the inner membrane and is lethal. Expression of the lptA-lptB operon is controlled by sigma-E.

document.description: LptB (formerly YhbG) is the nucleotide-binding domain (NBD) subunit of the LptB2FG ABC transporter of the Escherichia coli inner membrane. Two LptB copies form a homodimeric ATPase that sits on the cytoplasmic face of the inner membrane, docked onto the coupling helices of the transmembrane subunits LptF and LptG; the bitopic protein LptC associates with LptB2FG to form the LptB2FGC inner membrane complex. ATP binding and hydrolysis by LptB drive conformational changes in LptFG that extract newly synthesized lipopolysaccharide (LPS) from the outer leaflet of the inner membrane (after MsbA has flipped it) and push it into the periplasmic LptC-LptA-LptD protein bridge, which delivers LPS to the LptDE translocon for insertion into the outer leaflet of the outer membrane. LptB is essential; its depletion or catalytic inactivation (E163Q) blocks LPS transport and outer membrane biogenesis. Unlike classical ABC transporters, LptB2FG does not move its substrate across the bilayer but extrudes it out of the membrane.

document.description: LptC (formerly YrbK) is an essential bitopic inner-membrane protein of the seven-component lipopolysaccharide transport (Lpt) machinery of Escherichia coli. It has a single N-terminal transmembrane helix and a periplasmic beta-jellyroll domain that resembles LptA. LptC forms a tight complex with the ABC transporter LptB2FG, inserting its transmembrane helix between the LptF and LptG transmembrane domains, where it modulates transporter ATPase activity. The N-terminal edge of its beta-jellyroll contacts the periplasmic beta-jellyrolls of LptF/LptG. LPS extracted from the outer leaflet of the inner membrane by ATP hydrolysis is passed into the LptC beta-jellyroll and then to LptA, which docks on the C-terminal edge of LptC. Transfer is unidirectional, as LptA can displace LPS from LptC but not the reverse. Through LptA, LptC links the inner-membrane extractor to the outer-membrane LptDE translocon in a continuous trans-envelope bridge. Depletion of LptC blocks LPS delivery to the outer membrane, causes envelope defects and is lethal.

document.description: LptD (formerly Imp/OstA) is an essential 87 kDa integral outer-membrane protein of Escherichia coli and the beta-barrel subunit of the LptDE lipopolysaccharide (LPS) translocon. It has an N-terminal periplasmic beta-jellyroll domain, of the same OstA fold as LptA and LptC, and a C-terminal 26-stranded beta-barrel, the two linked by two interdomain disulfide bonds (Cys31-Cys724 and Cys173-Cys725), at least one of which is needed for function. The outer-membrane lipoprotein LptE sits inside the barrel as a plug. The jellyroll domain docks the C-terminus of periplasmic LptA, completing the LptB2FGC-LptA-LptD protein bridge that spans the envelope and carries LPS from the inner membrane. Arriving LPS is thought to move its core oligosaccharide and O-antigen through the barrel lumen while lipid A enters the outer leaflet through a lateral gate between barrel strands 1 and 26. LptD is folded and inserted by the BAM complex with the help of SurA, Skp, DsbA, DsbC, BepA, LptE and the lipoprotein LptM. Partial loss of LptD increases outer-membrane permeability to detergents, antibiotics, dyes, large maltodextrins and n-hexane; depletion blocks delivery of new LPS to the cell surface and is lethal.

core_functions.description: LptD is the outer-membrane beta-barrel subunit of the LptDE translocon. Its N-terminal periplasmic beta-jellyroll docks LptA and receives LPS from the periplasmic Lpt bridge. document.description: LptE (formerly RlpB, "rare lipoprotein B") is an essential outer-membrane lipoprotein of Escherichia coli and the plug subunit of the LptDE lipopolysaccharide (LPS) translocon. It is triacylated at its N-terminal cysteine and delivered to the inner leaflet of the outer membrane by the Lol pathway. About three quarters of LptE sits inside the lumen of the 26-stranded LptD beta-barrel, forming a two-protein plug-and-barrel complex in 1:1 stoichiometry. LptE has two roles. First, it is needed for LptD biogenesis: it engages LptD while BAM assembles it, stabilizes the barrel, and drives the disulfide rearrangement that yields functional, correctly oxidized LptD. Second, it binds LPS directly through conserved basic surface loops and can disrupt LPS-LPS interactions, which may help LPS insertion into the outer leaflet. Depletion of LptE stops newly made LPS from reaching the cell surface, raises outer-membrane permeability, and is lethal.

document.summary: LptD proteins are the outer-membrane component of the lipopolysaccharide transport (Lpt) system of diderm bacteria. Each has an N-terminal periplasmic beta-jellyroll domain that joins the LptA bridge and a C-terminal 26-stranded beta-barrel that, with the plug lipoprotein LptE, forms the LptD/LptE translocon. LPS arriving through the bridge is released through a lateral opening of the barrel into the outer leaflet of the outer membrane. In Escherichia coli LptD (formerly Imp/OstA) is essential and was first noticed through mutations that increase outer-membrane permeability to organic solvents and antibiotics. The family is a single PANTHER subfamily and its distribution tracks diderm bacteria with an outer membrane.

document.summary: This family contains LptF and LptG, the two paralogous transmembrane subunits of the LptB2FG ATP-binding cassette transporter that extracts lipopolysaccharide (LPS) from the outer leaflet of the inner membrane of diderm bacteria. LptF and LptG each have six transmembrane helices and a periplasmic beta-jellyroll domain; together they form a V-shaped cavity that LPS enters laterally from the membrane, and ATP hydrolysis by the cytoplasmic LptB dimer drives LPS out of the cavity into the LptC/LptA/LptD bridge. Both proteins are essential in Escherichia coli, where they were identified as the missing transmembrane components of the Lpt transporter (formerly YjgP and YjgQ). PANTHER separates the gammaproteobacterial LptF (SF7) and LptG (SF2) subfamilies from SF6 and SF8, which hold both paralogues from other phyla. The family name is taken from the Synechocystis member Slr0882.

document.summary: LptA proteins are periplasmic beta-jellyroll proteins of the lipopolysaccharide transport (Lpt) system of diderm bacteria. Head-to-tail oligomers of LptA connect the beta-jellyroll of the inner-membrane protein LptC to the N-terminal beta-jellyroll of the outer-membrane translocon LptD, forming a continuous hydrophobic groove through which LPS molecules are pushed across the periplasm. In Escherichia coli LptA is essential, binds LPS, and its depletion causes LPS to accumulate in the inner membrane. The family consists of a single PANTHER subfamily and its members share this bridging role wherever the remaining Lpt components are present.

document.summary: An ABC (ATP-binding cassette) nucleotide-binding-domain family of bacteria and archaea. All members are cytoplasmic ATPase subunits that dock onto the transmembrane domains of an inner-membrane ABC transporter and couple ATP binding and hydrolysis to transport. Two functionally distinct groups are well characterized. The LivG/LivF/BraF-type subunits (SF11, SF7 and related subfamilies) energize binding-protein-dependent uptake of branched-chain and other neutral amino acids. The LptB subfamily (SF10) energizes the LptB2FG transporter, which extracts lipopolysaccharide from the inner membrane and pushes it into the periplasmic Lpt bridge; LptB is essential in Escherichia coli, and ATP hydrolysis by LptB is required for LPS transport. Substrate and pathway therefore differ by subfamily, while ATPase activity and inner-membrane association are shared.
document.coherence_reason: The family lumps amino-acid uptake ATPases (LivG/LivF/BraF, SF11 and SF7; branched-chain amino acid ATPases of archaea, SF5 and SF8) with the LPS-export ATPase LptB (SF10). Transport substrate and direction cannot be propagated family-wide; only the ABC ATPase activity and membrane association are shared.
